assertions: The ship is lost and will not return safely — it has suffered wreck / sinking at sea
The principal significator in the 4th house and afflicted points to the end of the matter in loss, the ship gone to the bottom / not recoverable

The cargo and the merchant's money/goods aboard are lost with the ship — Mars in his fall near the cusp of the 2nd, afflicted retrograde Jupiter in the 2nd, and Part of Fortune in the 6th squared by Jupiter and the Moon
No good news of the ship will arrive; the long silence / no news is itself the sign, and any tidings to come will confirm loss rather than safety

The crew are in mortal danger / the voyage ends with death or grave harm — Moon separated from square of Saturn, lord of the 8th, then void of course, then to opposition of Mercury, lord of the 12th and 4th, Mercury in detriment and entering combustion
method: Classical horary astrology (Lilly, Christian Astrology Book II, ship question)
reasoning: Every testimony is afflicted with no saving testimony: Moon lately square Saturn lord of 8th/9th, then void of course, then to opposition of Mercury lord of 12th/4th in detriment and entering combustion; Mercury's dispositor Jupiter subterranean, conjunct Mars, retrograde and afflicted in the 2nd and square both Moon and Part of Fortune; Part of Fortune itself in the unfortunate 6th; Mars in fall near 2nd cusp threatens the merchant's substance; principal significator in the 4th (end of matter, grave/bottom) and afflicted. In Lilly's ship doctrine this convergence — 8th/12th/4th lords afflicting Moon and significator, Fortune cadent and afflicted, no benefic reception or application — judges loss of ship and goods, not delay or safe arrival.
summary: The ship is lost — sunk/wrecked with its cargo, and will not come home safe.
